definition: Categorizing audio by genre, mood, or instrument — the umbrella MIR classification task.
details: Categorizing audio by genre, mood, or instrument — the umbrella MIR classification task.

explainer.lead: Music classification is the umbrella MIR task of assigning labels such as genre, mood, or instrument to audio. It matters because those labels drive how music is organised, searched, and recommended.

tiers.eli5: Like sorting a big pile of songs into labelled boxes — this one is jazz, this one is sad, this one has a guitar.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train audio embeddings and classifiers on labelled track datasets, then use the predicted tags downstream. A pitfall is that mood and genre labels are subjective, so annotator disagreement caps achievable accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: Map an audio signal to one or more labels from a fixed set, typically by learning features and a classifier that outputs a probability per label. Accuracy is bounded by label noise and dataset coverage.

explainer.example: A track is fed to a classifier that outputs genre 'electronic' at 0.82 and mood 'energetic' at 0.71, and those tags are stored in the catalogue.
